subject: Evaluation milestones & commercial checkpoint — pricing, true-ups, and ramp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@fincorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-02-18 15:12 -05:00
Subject: Proposed eval plan + commercial milestones (first pass)

Clara — great speaking earlier. As discussed, I put together a suggested evaluation plan that ties MAP milestones to commercial checkpoints so we can align timing, commitments, and pricing. Key points:  

- 4-week PoC (week 1 internal integration, week 2 subset evaluation, week 3 performance/latency testing, week 4 QA & stakeholder demo)
- Success criteria: 95th-pct latency < 450ms p50 < 120ms (prod-like dataset), end-to-end accuracy on key prompts >= 86% against your acceptance set, < 2% error rate for tool-calls
- Commercial milestones: commit to 3 months initial reserved capacity (X tokens/month) on go-live OR 12-month usage-based commit after PoC for 20% discount; ramp credits tied to on-time completion of milestones
- Pricing protection: propose price lock for 12 months from contract signature for committed tiers; true-up quarterly for overage with 30-day invoice cycle

Can you confirm these maps to your timeline and call out any procurement/legal must-haves we should bake into the MAP (e.g., exact true-up cadence, definition of billable usage)? I attached a first-pass MAP spreadsheet and a short doc that proposes definitions.

Next step: if the PoC timeline looks good, Karthik and I can sync with Rahul and your procurement on the commercial terms and get Laura to run a quick review of the SOW redlines.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: FinCorp_MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), usage_definitions.docx (definitions)

From: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@fincorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@fincorp.com>
Date: 2026-02-19 09:03 -05:00
Subject: Re: Proposed eval plan + commercial milestones (first pass)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and close to what we discussed. A few procurement/legal items we need clarified before we can commit:  

1) True-up cadence: we prefer semi-annual true-ups (vs quarterly) with a single reconciliation invoice to avoid frequent billing spikes. Can you accommodate?
2) Price protection: procurement wants a 12-month price protection from the effective date, and a cap on any increase for non-committed tiers (we can discuss exact %).
3) Definition of billable usage: your "token" definition needs to map to our internal usage metric; please confirm whether embeddings, tool-calls, and streaming are all billed consistently. We need a plain-language definition in the SOW.
4) Ramp credits/discounts: we like the idea of credits tied to MAP milestones, but need the formula (e.g., X% credit on month N invoices if milestone completed on time) and whether credits offset committed usage or only overage.

Procurement (Rahul) is on copy — he'll coordinate the formal redlines but wanted to make the high-level asks clear. Can Karthik/Marissa propose concrete language for true-ups and price protection so procurement can circulate to legal?

Best,
Clara
Director, Data Platform — FinCorp
clara.nguyen@fincorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-02-20 11:18 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed eval plan + commercial milestones (procurement asks)

Team — forwarding procurement feedback from FinCorp (see below). Short asks from legal/procurement: semi-annual true-ups preferred, clarified billable usage, explicit 12-month price protection, and clear ramp-credit mechanics.

Question for legal: is semi-annual true-up acceptable from our side given reserved capacity and committed discounts? Also, we need specific SOW language for "billable usage" (tokens vs inference-unit) that is defensible.

Karthik — can you propose the commercial compromise? My suggestion:  
- Keep quarterly true-ups but amortize invoices if FinCorp wants a single reconciliation document (we can present as an implementation detail) OR agree to semi-annual true-ups with a 5% premium on committed discount to mitigate price exposure.
- For price protection: 12-month price lock on committed tiers; variable tiers can adjust with 60-day notice but cap at +7% (proposal).
- Ramp credits: propose milestone credits that apply to future invoices (not to increase committed baseline). Example: complete PoC on-time -> $15k credit applied across the first 3 months of live usage.

Laura — any immediate redline language you recommend for definition of billable usage?

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-02-22 09:47 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed eval plan + commercial milestones (procurement asks)

Marissa/Karthik — quick legal POV:  

- True-up cadence: semi-annual is workable but increases revenue recognition lag; suggest compromise language that supports either cadence by defaulting to quarterly unless the customer elects semi-annual at signature (so customer choice). If customer picks semi-annual, we want a minimum committed notice and ability to invoice interim overages as credits to the next reconciliation.
- Price protection: standard 12-month lock OK for committed tiers. For non-committed (on-demand) usage, redline to require 60 days' written notice of price changes and cap increases at a defined percentage (we can propose 7%). Avoid open-ended language such as "subject to market changes".
- Definition of billable usage: propose the following short clause for the SOW: "Billable usage means: (i) tokens processed for text generation and completion requests; (ii) embedding vector counts based on input tokens; (iii) tool-calls that invoke external APIs or actions as separately metered operations; (iv) streaming is billed by tokens emitted, not socket time." Add cross-reference to usage_definitions.docx in the SOW.
- True-ups/true-up demo: require reconciliation statement, with ability to dispute within 30 days; late payments subject to standard interest.

I'll prepare redline snippets and attach as a PDF to the SOW.

-Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com

Attachment: SOW_redlines_20260222.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@fincorp.com>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@fincorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-02-24 16:05 -05:00
Subject: Revised MAP + commercial proposal (attached)

Clara / Rahul — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a revised MAP (FinCorp_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a redlined SOW that incorporates Laura's suggested language. Highlights of the commercial compromise:  

1) True-ups: default quarterly reconciliation. Customer may elect semi-annual reconciliation at signature. If semi-annual is selected, overages will be documented each quarter and netted at reconciliation (single invoice).

2) Price protection: 12-month price lock on committed tiers. On-demand tiers require 60 days' notice and are capped at +7% per year. We will include the cap in Section 4.2 of the SOW.

3) Billable usage: The SOW now contains a clear definition tied to the usage_definitions.docx. Embeddings and streaming billed by tokens; tool-calls separately metered. A summary table is in the MAP spreadsheet.

4) Ramp credits: milestone credits apply to invoiceable amounts for the first 90 days post-go-live (credits offset invoices rather than increase committed baseline). Example: PoC sign-off on-time = $15k credit spread across first three invoices.

5) Timing & close: PoC start target Mar 8, PoC complete Apr 5, go-live target May 3. We requested expedited legal review with a signature target by Mar 12 if PoC completes on schedule.

Please find: FinCorp_MAP_v2.xlsx, SOW_redlines_20260224.pdf, usage_definitions.docx attached. If procurement is comfortable with the compromise, Karthik and I can pull together a mutual action plan with calendar invites for milestone sign-offs.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com

Attachments: FinCorp_MAP_v2.xlsx; SOW_redlines_20260224.pdf; usage_definitions.docx

Date: 2026-02-26 09:03 -05:00
Subject: Re: Revised MAP + commercial proposal (attached)

Marissa — thanks for revising quickly. Procurement is broadly comfortable with the approach; two quick asks before we circulate to Finance/Legal:  

1) Can you make the reconciliation flow and invoice examples explicit in the MAP (sample numbers) so Finance can see cash impact?
2) Can we get a one-page summary of credits and how they apply to invoices (examples for both quarterly and semi-annual true-up)?

If you can drop those two artifacts into the shared Drive folder by EOD Monday, we should be able to get internal sign-off and schedule a short executive signature call. Would Mar 12 still be realistic if PoC completes on schedule?

Thanks —
Rahul Singh
Head of Procurement, FinCorp
